file: papers/pdf/McFarlane and Carter - 2016 - Serendipity and Its Role in the Discovery of Entrepreneurial Opportunities.pdf
about: A study of 21 Glasgow music entrepreneurs showing how serendipity (accident plus sagacity) bridges causal and effectual logic in identifying entrepreneurial opportunities.

candidates.label: Accident plus sagacity
candidates.definition: Serendipity is the gift of making discoveries by accident when a person connects with their environment; it is not mere luck but combines a chance event with prior knowledge.
candidates.applies_when: An account describes an accidental discovery that the person could recognise or use because of what they already knew.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Pure luck with no role for the person's knowledge or judgment in recognising the event.

candidates.label: Three interacting elements
candidates.definition: Following Dew, serendipity involves a resource (sagacity/prior knowledge), an event (contingency) and an activity (the person is already on a journey), plus sound judgment to decide if the event can be acted on.
candidates.applies_when: An account shows a chance event occurring while the person was already pursuing some activity, met with knowledge and a judgment to act.

candidates.label: Opportunity discovery spaces
candidates.definition: Dew's four spaces: systematic exploration of knowledge corridors, spontaneous recognition of new information, pre-discoveries (search plus contingency without relevant knowledge, so useless), and true serendipities.
candidates.applies_when: An account can be placed as systematic search, spontaneous recognition, an idea that could not be used for lack of knowledge, or full serendipity.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Pre-discovery: chance idea that is useless without relevant knowledge, as distinct from serendipity.

candidates.label: Chance encounter
candidates.definition: Unexpected meetings or being in the right place at the right time act as trigger events, such as discovering an artist in an audience or being told to come see a band.
candidates.applies_when: Person describes an unplanned meeting or happening to be present when something notable occurred.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Meetings deliberately sought through planned networking.

candidates.label: Accident or mistake
candidates.definition: Errors such as getting off at the wrong stop or knocking on the wrong door can lead to entry into a profession.
candidates.applies_when: Account attributes a career or venture path to a mistake or wrong turn.

candidates.label: Prior knowledge kicks in to exploit
candidates.definition: The activity is already underway when the contingency happens; insight arises when sagacity or prior experience helps the entrepreneur recognise and exploit it.
candidates.applies_when: Account shows the person using existing experience to turn a chance event into an opportunity (e.g., B.M. using industry experience to build Paolo Nutini into a brand).

candidates.label: Action, recognition and insight
candidates.definition: Serendipitous discoveries involve a mix of action, recognition and insight by the individual.
candidates.applies_when: Person describes acting, noticing and realising something during a chance discovery.

candidates.label: Effectual embracing of contingency
candidates.definition: Effectual entrepreneurs embrace unanticipated serendipities, asking what they can do with the means they have (who they are, what they know, whom they know), flexibly exploiting contingency.
candidates.applies_when: Person responds to an unexpected development by working with existing means, identity and contacts rather than a prior plan.

candidates.label: Networks and who you know
candidates.definition: Entrepreneurs build networks of stakeholders, mostly friendship-based, which offer opportunities and stability and are part of the means effectual entrepreneurs draw on.
candidates.applies_when: Account highlights friends or industry contacts as the base from which opportunities arose.

candidates.label: Industry experience
candidates.definition: Knowledge gained through work experience or education in the industry underpins recognising and exploiting opportunities.
candidates.applies_when: Person cites prior jobs or training as what let them see or use an opportunity.

candidates.label: Bridge between causation and effectuation
candidates.definition: Serendipity lies between planned and unplanned approaches: causation inspires the initial search, chance recognition creates fit between person and idea, and effectual logic then guides working with given means.
candidates.applies_when: Account shows a planned search, then an unexpected event producing a fit, then means-based development.

candidates.label: Redirecting the path
candidates.definition: Entrepreneurs may start with a plan but end up in other areas via a trigger such as luck, accident or chance encounter.
candidates.applies_when: Person searching for one thing finds another and changes direction.

candidates.label: Entry into the industry
candidates.definition: Chance events can provide entry into a profession or venture, as with E.P.'s entry via the wrong door.
candidates.applies_when: Account credits starting a career or venture to a chance event.

candidates.label: Systematic search
candidates.definition: The literature holds that opportunities more likely result from systematic search and that attributing discoveries to luck overlooks preparation (education, analysis, persistence).
candidates.applies_when: Account explains an opportunity as arising from deliberate planned search or progression (e.g., band to college to business, spotting a gap while employed).
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Cases where an unplanned contingency was decisive.

candidates.label: Mere luck
candidates.definition: Attributing discoveries to dumb luck or coincidence alone, which authors argue serendipity is not, since it relies on prior knowledge.
candidates.applies_when: Account frames an outcome as pure luck with no contribution from the person.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Luck combined with recognition grounded in knowledge (serendipity).

candidates.label: Right place, right time narrative
candidates.definition: Entrepreneurs narrate pivotal events as being in the right place at the right time or 'all down to choosing the wrong door'.
candidates.applies_when: Person narrates a pivotal moment using luck or timing idioms.

candidates.label: Dense creative industry context
candidates.definition: Serendipity occurs continually within the music industry, especially in Glasgow, where chance encounters are central for all interviewees.
candidates.applies_when: Account links chance encounters to working in a dense local creative scene.

candidates.label: Uncertainty and lack of career paths
candidates.definition: Turbulent environments and undefined career paths push entrepreneurs to adapt, build portfolio careers and decide based on affordable loss, favouring effectual exploitation of contingency.
candidates.applies_when: Person describes uncertainty or lacking a clear path as prompting them to adapt and take what comes.
